newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany urges EU calm over Iran envoy row.
newsitem.headline: Germany urges EU calm over Iran envoy row.

text.p: Germany's deputy foreign minister on Sunday said European Union countries should remain calm in a diplomatic row with Iran over its refusal to accept the return of the German and Danish ambassadors to Tehran.
"We should be cool and level-headed in this situation," Werner Hoyer, state secretary in the foreign ministry, told German radio.

Hoyer said the EU states should not allow Tehran to drive a wedge between them. "We should not allow ourselves to be divided," he said. "The EU has made it clear that they (the ambassadors) will only return together."
Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Thursday denounced Iran's refusal to accept the return of the German envoy and said his country would not submit to "blackmail".
Iran said on Wednesday neither the German and Danish ambassadors were welcome back in the country after the EU agreed to send its envoys back.
The EU initially withdrew its ambassadors last month after a German court implicated Iranian leaders in the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

Hoyer said Iran should make it clear whether the two countries had diplomatic relations or not. "Either one has diplomatic relations or not. There is no grey area in which one can move around," he said.
